findings.description: AC-1 lists com.google.code.gson:gson:2.14.0 as a main dependency of NaruServe-gson but does not fix its scope, and the Implementation Note says api vs implementation is an implementer choice except for TinyHttpd. D-196 (wave 5) makes GsonJsonCodec accept a caller-built Gson, so Gson is in that module's public signature. D-228/D-197 have the bootstrap build the default Gson (Strictness.STRICT, disableJdkUnsafe). If wave 1 picks implementation, callers of the D-196 constructor and the bootstrap (whose AC-1 list is 'exactly' and has no direct gson edge) cannot compile against Gson. The fix would then be a main-dependency change in a later wave, which the D-005 run-end check against the AC-1/AC-2 graph rejects.
findings.suggested_action: In AC-1 (or a new AC), fix NaruServe-gson -> gson:2.14.0 as api scope, traced to D-196 and D-228. Narrow the Implementation Note's 'implementation choice' to edges that do not appear in a public signature.

findings.description: AC-2 only requires that the root build applies a Kotlin Gradle Plugin 2.x and that Kotlin test sources compile. No AC says which modules get the plugin. Later waves add Kotlin tests: D-349 needs every docs/api Kotlin example as a Kotlin test, D-351 adds nullable-accessor tests and D-355 adds a default Gson codec test (T11). If wave 1 applies KGP only to the module that hosts the smoke test, those waves must apply a plugin to more modules. The SRS treats a later plugin addition as a D-005 violation: CON-BUILD-006 AC-8 and its note pre-apply java-test-fixtures so that 'the run-end D-005 check sees no new plugin'. So KGP is left out of a rule the SRS itself applies.
findings.suggested_action: Add an AC (OPS-BUILD-002 or CON-BUILD-004) saying the root build.gradle applies KGP 2.x in wave 1 to every module of CON-BUILD-002 AC-1, or at least to every module that will host Kotlin tests, traced to D-005 and D-023. Keep CON-BUILD-007 (kotlin.stdlib.default.dependency=false) as the guard.

findings.description: AC-1 says the property defaults to /Users/beom/work/git/TinyHttpd 'when not set on the command line or in gradle.properties', but the trace links name gradle.properties as an implementing file. If the implementer writes the default into the project gradle.properties, the default case of AC-1 can no longer be observed, and the AC cannot tell a code default from a gradle.properties value.
findings.suggested_action: Say where the default lives, for example: settings.gradle supplies the default when no Gradle property of that name is set (-P, project or user gradle.properties). Or drop the gradle.properties trace link from OPS-BUILD-001.
